name: AI in Testing Gap Analyzer & Optimizer
tag: Compares how your QA team uses AI with common industry practice and gives a plan to close the gaps.

scenarios.title: Benchmark a QA team
scenarios.ask: Benchmark our QA team of {testers}. About {auto}% of tests are automated and we use AI in {areas} of 6 practice areas.
steps: Survey
Scored 6 practice areas: test design, data generation, self-healing scripts, visual checks, defect triage and reporting.
Benchmark
Compared your answers with a sample peer profile of mid-size software teams.
Gap finder
Found {=6 - areas} areas where AI is not used yet. Largest gap: test data generation.
Optimizer
Ranked fixes by effort and payoff for a team of {testers}.
followups: Where does the peer median come from?
It is a sample benchmark built into the demo. In a real engagement we calibrate it with your industry and team size, and we show the source.
Is a higher score always better?
No. The score shows where you could use AI, not where you must. Some areas, like exploratory testing, often stay mostly human.

scenarios.title: Cut flaky tests
scenarios.ask: {flaky}% of our {suite} UI tests fail randomly. Show how AI tools could help.
steps: Log reader
Grouped {=round(suite * flaky / 100)} flaky tests by failure message.
Root-cause agent
{=round(flaky * 5)}% of flaky failures trace to changed element locators, a pattern self-healing tools target.
Optimizer
Proposed self-healing locators, smarter waits and quarantine for the worst 20 tests.
Estimator
Projected the flaky rate after 8 weeks if the plan is followed.
followups: Do self-healing locators hide real bugs?
They can if left unchecked. The plan logs every healed locator for review, so a real UI change is still seen by a person.
Most of the gain comes from the worst few dozen tests, so teams often see fewer reruns within the first two sprints.

scenarios.title: Build a 90-day roadmap
scenarios.ask: We have {budget} dollars a month for tools and {hours} hours a week to spare. Build a 90-day plan.
steps: Gap list
Loaded the gaps from your last assessment.
Optimizer
Fit work into {=hours * 13} team-hours over 13 weeks and ${budget} a month.
Sequencer
Ordered steps so each one makes the next easier: test data first, then triage, then visual checks.
Writer
Wrote a week-by-week plan with a measurable goal for each month.
followups: What if our budget is zero?
The plan leans on open-source tools and the AI features already in your test platform. Fewer initiatives fit, but test data generation is usually still possible.
Can we re-run the assessment at day 90?
Yes. The second run shows your score change area by area against the first.
